story_text.value:
Hello HN!

My name is Sam and this is Craig. Craig is a local-first TUI for managing AI coding agents. It’s agent-agnostic, creates isolated worktrees by default, and has a rich CLI for the agent to interact with to manipulate state and perform actions in the TUI.

I started building Craig when I got a job offer at a shop that was using Cursor. I was previously using Claude Code with Conductor and really enjoyed this type of experience. However Conductor didn’t support Cursor at the time and I wasn’t a big fan of the Cursor 3 Agents interface. For personal projects I was using mostly Codex with some Claude Code. Switching between tooling was frustrating. Around the same time I also started really enjoying the agent CLIs and how they just “felt good”.

Craig kind of builds on that and I think of it as a heads-up display and controls around the CLI. With the TUI being keyboard-driven you can get into a nice multi-task flow and move around pretty quickly. The UX is made to be low friction and high signal-to-noise.

To get started you can run `npm install -g craig-cli`, launch your favorite terminal (I like Ghostty), pop it in fullscreen and run the `craig` command. Once you launch it you can create a workspace, this can be a single repo directory or multiple. Then create a new task under the workspace to launch Cursor, Codex, or Claude. Do your thang, and use your agent to create a PR. You’ll see Craig automatically sync that PR, poll for checks and let you know when the PR is ready to merge. Merge it and keep moving in the same thread or start a new one.

I’d love for you to give it a try and let me know what you think - any feedback is greatly appreciated.

title.value: Show HN: Craig – A TUI for running parallel coding agents

story_text.value:
Vibetown is a site where you can create a public sandbox (shoutout fly.io sprites / machines) that anyone can contribute to with their AI agents. You can also get matched with a random person in a sandbox to vibe code with them, and if you like what you built then you can open it up and keep it running! Think of it something like twitch meets lovable. There is a chat in each room, along with a localhost preview. People take turns connecting their Claude Code subscriptions and making any changes to the app. Sandboxes automatically go to sleep after a while, but can be woken up. It's completely free because right now I'm only supporting frontend apps. Use it to create art or cool websites without anything fancy. In the future, I will add database, AI (api), and other integrations.

The short-term goal is just to see how people collaborate with strangers on public apps. The long-term goal is to make it possible for indie devs to build fully working apps with others that actually generate revenue.

Let me know what you think! I have 4 public sandboxes running right now that anyone can hop in and contribute to.

title.value: Show HN: Vibetown – public sandboxes to vibecode with strangers

story_text.value: Hi my name is Quinn, and I have been testing and using LLMs for various coding projects for about a year now. And at this point I run all my agents overnight or for even days at a time. And I’ve sunk countless hours and tokens into coming back to a job that's half done with issues and bugs. That's why I built Krites. It blocks the edit tools on the paths you name, runs your tests when your agent tries to stop and blocks the stop until they pass (up to 3 tries by default), and prints a receipt with /krites:receipt that contains commands, exit codes, diff and commit. The known limits along with more in depth documentation are in the repo’s README. Install it with: claude plugin install krites@anthropic-plugin-directory. Comment if you have any questions, suggestions, comments or similar experiences.

title.value: Show HN: Krites, Claude Code Plugin that forces your tests to run

story_text.value:
pi-cowboy is an agent orchestrator for Pi(https://pi.dev) and Herdr(https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr). Break large jobs into focused subtasks, hand them off to background agents running in parallel, and consolidate the results when they finish. Each agent runs in an isolated copy-on-write Git work-tree, minimising disk overhead.

pi-cowboy can orchestrate foreign harnesses too, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and more.

Feature highlights:

- Foreign harnesses: pi-cowboy agents can run in Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pig and Pi-Bolt, as well as Pi. This gives you great flexibility in choosing how to spend your tokens. Running out of Codex usage? Switch your pi-cowboy harness to OpenCode, select one of its free models, and let it handle the rest. Pig and Pi-Bolt are pi variants that are more efficient, with a lower memory footprint and faster performance than pi. Because pi-cowboy is designed to run multiple agents in parallel, having a lower per-agent footprint is crucial. It prevents your machine from running out of resources and lets you have higher concurrency without choking your system.

- Concurrency limits: You can configure concurrency limits at every level. Running a local model with limited resources? If a simple task already takes hours to complete, the last thing you want is to overload your machine by running too many of them at once. Set concurrency limits for that model specifically to keep resource usage under control.

You can install it on Pi as a package:

  pi install npm:pi-cowboy #(requires `herdr` 0.8+)

title.value: Show HN: Pi-cowboy – use Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode as subagents

story_text.value: MeetCap records your meetings, transcribes them on your computer, and works with your AI agent in both directions. Your agent can run it. In Claude Code, Codex or any agent that can load a skill, say "record this meeting" and the menu bar icon turns into a red dot. The agent can also stop the recording, name speakers, get the minutes, and search past meetings. It can run your agent. Pick one you already use and MeetCap calls it in the background to write the live summaries and the minutes, on the subscription you already pay for. It works with 20+ agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI and Qwen Code. No agent? Use your own API key, or let MeetCap download a local model. Speech recognition, live captions, speaker diarization and recognizing voices you've named all run on your computer, and recording, captions and diarization keep going offline. With the local model, the summaries and minutes are written on your computer too, so not even the text leaves it. During the call you get a summary every few minutes, with background on terms you might not know. Afterward, each point in the minutes links to the transcript line it came from, and you can play the audio back from there. Transcripts and minutes are Markdown files in a folder you pick. The app and the command line are free, with no account and no time limits. macOS 14.2 or later, Apple silicon or Intel: curl -fsSL https://meetcap.seacen.dev/install.sh | bash That installs the app, the meetcap command, and the MeetCap skill for each agent it finds on your computer. Or download it from https://meetcap.seacen.dev/download/

title.value: Show HN: MeetCap – Free on-device meeting transcription your AI agent can run
